title: Nanobatch unit-econ scratchpad (tokens, batching, quick tiers)
content:
Context / what this is: quick personal scratchpad for an idea: small request aggregation ("nanobatching") + hybrid PAYG + commit tiers. Aim: cut per-token GPU wall-clock and cash cost for many low-latency short calls. Notes are informal, rough numbers, lots of open questions.

Assumptions (baseline):
- Model: 13B quantized, throughput approx 120 tokens/sec on chosen infra (inference-optimized).
- HW amortized cost (fixed plus variable): $6.50 / hour effective per GPU (including infra + ops amortized in committed pools).
- Average session size for target app: 400 prompt tokens + 150 generated tokens = 550 tokens per request.
- API overhead + routing: ~5ms per request, negligible for batching math but matters for SLO.

Key micro-ideas:
1) Nanobatch: hold very short window (e.g., 8–12ms) to collect requests into tiny batches before scheduling. Preserves low tail latency if we gate on request count + time.
2) Prefix cache reuse band: many requests share common prefixes (system prompts). Leverage KV-cache reuse to avoid recompute for prefix tokens.
3) Tiering by burst vs steady: free/dev PAYG allowed to nanobatch; premium paid customers get dedicated capacity or lower nanobatch wait (SLA).

Simple math: per-token server capacity and cost approximations
- Tokens/sec per GPU = 120 (assumption)
- Cost per hour per GPU = $6.50 -> cost per second = $6.50/3600 = $0.0018056/sec
- Cost per token = cost_per_sec / tokens_per_sec = 0.0018056 / 120 ≈ $1.5046e-05 (0.0015 cents) per token

Per request cost (no batching, full tokens served)
- 550 tokens * $0.000015046 ≈ $0.008275 (≈ 0.83 cents)
- So 1k requests ~ $8.27; 100k requests ~ $827

Effect of nanobatch: if we batch N concurrent similar-latency requests into one forward pass with shared prefix (idealized):
- Suppose each request has prefix of 200 tokens shared, unique continuation 350 tokens. If we can compute prefix once (KV reuse) and only do tail per request, we reduce work.
- Ideal batching of M requests for tail: total tokens processed ≈ prefix_tokens + M * tail_tokens (assuming perfect prefix reuse and combined attention cost little extra).
- Example M=8: tokens processed ≈ 200 + 8*350 = 200 + 2800 = 3000 tokens vs 8*550=4400 tokens -> 32% token work reduction.
- Cost per request under M=8 approximates: (3000 tokens * cost_per_token) / 8 ≈ (3000*0.000015046)/8 ≈ $0.00564 (~0.56 cents) -> ~32% cheaper than no-batch.

Overhead and realism notes:
- Not every request shares 200 prefix tokens; many will have short prompts. Benefit varies by product.
- Latency: holding for M=8 will add additional queuing delay. If arrival rate low, waiting for M triggers SLO tradeoffs. Use both time cap and max-count cap.
- Implementation complexity: requires request coalescing at routing layer + KV cache coordination. Danger: pathological tail if many long-running completions.

Pricing ramifications / tier ideas (sketch):
A) Free/dev tier (encourages experimentation): small monthly free token allotment (e.g., 250k tokens), PAYG after that at public rate, but these requests are eligible for nanobatch queuing (longer queue allowed up to 25ms).
B) Developer PAYG tier: $0.004 per 1k tokens (intro rate) with nanobatch optimization applied for avg queue < 20ms. No commitments.
C) Startup commit plan: $X/month reserved capacity credits (example $1,000/mo) gives higher throughput and dedicated spot in nanobatch pipelines (lower queue), credits burn at discounted unit rate (e.g., 20% off list).
D) Enterprise / Dedicated: flat eGPU reservation + per-token internal accounting. Can disable nanobatch or set strict SLOs.

Sample unit-econ per 100k monthly active users (MAU) scenario - quick back of envelope
- Assume each MAU generates 15 requests/day -> 1.5M requests/mo -> avg tokens per request 550 -> monthly tokens = 825M tokens
- At baseline cost_per_token approx 0.000015046 -> infra cost = 825,000,000 * 0.000015046 ≈ $12,396
- With nanobatch + prefix reuse savings 25% -> cost = $9,297 -> savings $3.1k/mo -> meaningful at scale
- Revenue examples: if we price at $0.004/1k tokens -> revenue = 825,000 * 0.004 = $3,300 -> gross margin negative at list price; need commit discounts or higher price or higher batching to reach profitability.

Observations / next experiments to run (practical):
- Instrument token-level prefix similarity metric on production traces (what fraction of requests share >100 prefix tokens?). This determines theoretical maximum of prefix reuse.
- Build microbench: simulate arrival patterns, run nanobatch hold window sweep (2ms, 5ms, 10ms, 20ms), measure tail p95 added latency and batch size distribution.
- Cost modeling: add GPU preemption, memory pressure, KV-cache hit rate, and cooling/healing ops overheads.
- Pricing experiments: test two axes in checkerboard rollout: (a) unit price per 1k tokens; (b) committed discount + reserved throughput. Measure churn and expansion.

Open questions / friction points:
- Are enterprise customers comfortable with nanobatch-induced jitter? likely need controls to opt-out.
- Billing accuracy for partially shared compute (how to account when prefix cached): charge full tokens or discounted rate? Could have a "compute-shared discount" applied when system detects cached prefix reuse.
- Legal / tax if we give deep discounts mid-contract. Need simple transparent rules.

Short-term action items (personal):
- Ask infra for per-GPU effective cost numbers (including ops) and realistic tokens/sec for 13B & 30B quantized variants.
- Pull recent 7-day token histograms from API logs (bucketed by session length).
- Prototype nanobatch simulator with arrival traces (small python sim).

Notes-to-self: keep wording simple in pitch decks: "Nanobatch = small intentional delay to dramatically reduce per-token cost for high-cardinality short requests". Emphasize opt-out and SLA controls.

End of scratchpad. Many rough edges; delete or version as needed.
